detail.body:
> **Draft for review, not intended to merge as is.** This PR is one of a bundle of model ports, each passing its verification gates on its own. Some of them change shared code (checkpoint conversion hooks, patches, model bases) in overlapping ways. A second code-reuse round will consolidate that shared code across the bundle and resubmit as a sequence of smaller PRs: shared infrastructure first, then each model on top. Review comments on correctness are most useful now; comments on structure and reuse will feed that round.

## Summary

Adds the **text decoder** of `meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B` (revision `0fb02478b025`) to Primus. Primer, an agent that onboards models to Primus, generated this change from run `Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-20261025-212640-683e` and verified it on `main` at `dad0a081af43`. It is a draft for maintainer review.

## Scope

This pull request adds Muse Spark Open's **text decoder** (`text_config`, model type `muse_spark_text`): 62 layers, an 816B-total / ~42B-active mixture of experts, text in and text out. The checkpoint converter maps only the text decoder (`model.language_model.*` and `lm_head`).

Muse Spark Open itself is multimodal (text, image, video and audio in; text out). Its other components are **not part of this pull request** and are planned as follow-ups:

- **Vision tower:** a 50-layer ViT with window attention and 2D RoPE, and a 2×2 merge of image patches (images and video).
- **Vision projector:** the adapter and projection that merge image features into the text embeddings.
- **Audio tower:** a 4-stage causal convolution encoder on the raw waveform.

With this pull request, the text decoder trains on text, and fine-tuning starts from the released checkpoint through Primus's checkpoint hook. **Updated (current port):** the vocabulary is padded to 202,048 at every TP, the released router expert-bias correction is kept, and fine-tuning from the converted checkpoint is verified on a 4-layer cut of the released weights (the hook converts it, Megatron loads it, and the first loss is far below a random model's). The full 816B model has no distributed converter: the hook stops with an error that lists the supported routes (convert on a host with about 3.3 TB of RAM by raising `native_ckpt_max_params`, or point `pretrained_checkpoint` at a `torch_dist` checkpoint made elsewhere); see the hook's README section. Image, video and audio inputs need the follow-up above.

**Verified on the current port:** static checks and lint; per-layer and full-model log-prob parity with the Hugging Face reference; training (end to end, proxy, the parallel layouts the plan requires); the checkpoint save/reload round trip; fine-tuning from the checkpoint (4-layer cut); 10-node training; and data-parallel scale-out of the full configuration to 960 GPUs.

**Open review items being worked on:** the launcher's MASTER_PORT probe (stderr captured with the port; ports set outside `--env` not treated as pinned; and whether that generic launcher change belongs in this PR), `remove_partial_checkpoint` deleting the latest-iteration marker of a complete checkpoint, and a fallback in the FLOPs patch that CI never exercises.

## Testing

### What was verified, in plain terms

This change was written and tested by Primer, an internal AMD agent that onboards models to Primus (to be open-sourced; until then this note explains its checks). Primer runs a fixed ladder of checks on real MI355X GPUs, each one stricter than the last. The levels (L0 to L7) in the table below mean:

| Level | What it checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | **Static checks:** the new configs load the way Primus loads them, presets and experiments exist for MI300X and MI355X, the model is registered | pass (a stricter version, which also checks that every layer is built on Megatron's own blocks, flags the four norm classes; being addressed) |
| L1 | **Layer math:** each layer's outputs and gradients match the Hugging Face reference implementation on the released weights (17 model-specific checks: embeddings, attention, MoE routing, norms, residual gates, long context, held-out tokens) | pass |
| L2 | **Kernels:** the fused kernels the layers use (RoPE, attention, router, norms, logit softcap) match a plain reference at the model's shapes, forward and backward | pass |
| L3 | **Whole-model numerics:** the released weights loaded into this Primus model give the same next-token log-probabilities as `transformers` (max difference 1.8e-5, limit 1e-3), and the architecture matches the checkpoint's config | pass (on a 4-layer cut of the model; the full model is pending, below) |
| L4 | **Training:** the trainer test runs, a short training run gives the same losses with tensor parallelism 1 and 2, and training gives the same losses in 13 parallel layouts: pipeline (plain and interleaved), tensor + sequence, context, expert, combined, distributed optimizer, Megatron-FSDP, full and selective recompute | pass |
| L7 | **Multi-node training:** the full configuration trained on 10 MI355X nodes | pending (see Notes) |

L5 and L6 (long convergence runs, checkpoint conversion with lm-eval) are not part of this change.

### Primer's raw record

Primer's verification ladder in run `Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-20261025-212640-683e` (stopped): L0, L1, L2, L3, L4 reached.

- **L0 Static:** The YAML the port adds loads the way Primus loads it: it parses, every extends target exists, override keys are known, and the new model has an experiment per platform and a trainer test entry.
- **L1 Layer math:** Each layer of the port against the reference implementation, through the Verifier's validated checks.
- **L2 Op parity on one GPU:** The kernels the port's layers run, at the model's shapes and settings, forward and backward against eager PyTorch, including ragged and tail shapes, warm allocator replay, guard zones and poisoned torch.empty: l2-op-parity on the op specs the Verifier writes and validates.
- **L3 Numeric parity:** The port's architecture matches the checkpoint's config, and the released weights loaded into the port give the same next-token log-probabilities as transformers.
- **L4 Training bar:** The port trains: the trainer test entry runs as written, and a short proxy run gives the same losses in two tensor-parallel layouts.

Lint: Primus's pre-commit hooks pass on the changed files (`pre-commit run --files`; `thirdparty-lock` skipped, it needs the submodules).

## Notes for reviewers

- Verification: the run's round-3 port passed every single-node rung in Primer's verifier pass (L0 static checks; L1/L2 model-specific checks, 17 of 17; L3 next-token log-probabilities against `transformers` within 1e-3 on the reduced cut; L4 trainer test, proxy training in TP1/TP2, and the parallel-training gate in 13 layouts: PP, interleaved PP, TP+SP, CP, EP, a combined layout, distributed optimizer, Megatron-FSDP, full and selective recompute). Its 10-node training check failed on a Primer harness bug (expert parallelism larger than the proxy's expert count), since fixed; the run was stopped there, so the table above is from that pass.
- **Full scale pending:** full-model L3 on 2 nodes and the full configuration trained on 10 MI355X nodes run now; this description is updated with the results.
- Left out of this PR: a patch that made Megatron's torch-FSDP2 path work for parameters kept in fp32 (Megatron-integration work, not this model's port). Megatron-FSDP and the distributed optimizer work without it.
- Formatting: Primus's pre-commit hooks (isort, autoflake, black) were applied to the generated code.

- Draft: Primus's lint CI runs now. Code owners are requested when it is marked ready for review, and GPU tests run once a maintainer adds `ci:gpu`.

+### 11.5 Muse Spark (`models/megatron/muse_spark/muse_spark_base.yaml`)
+
+These settings (YAML keys in `muse_spark_base.yaml`, and the environment variables marked (env)) apply only to a Muse Spark model (`model_type: muse_spark`).
+
+| Parameter | Default | Description |
+|-----------|---------|-------------|
+| `muse_spark_skip_memory_check` | `false` | *Primus:* `true` skips the `before_train` check that fails fast when weights + grads + optimizer states per GPU exceed GPU memory. A string is true for `1` / `true` / `yes` / `on` and false for `0` / `false` / `no` / `off` or empty (any case). Another value is false and gives a warning. |
+| `PRIMUS_TURBO_DEEPEP_INTERNODE` (env) | unset | *Primus:* Turbo DeepEP (`use_turbo_deepep`) runs only inside one node unless Primus-Turbo is built with rocSHMEM. When the expert group (expert TP x EP) spans more GPUs than one node has, Muse Spark turns DeepEP off and uses the `alltoall` dispatcher, with a warning. Set `1` / `true` / `yes` / `on` to keep DeepEP across nodes with a rocSHMEM build. At EP >= 16, `turbo_deepep_num_cu` must be <= 32. An environment variable, not a YAML key. |
+| `MUSE_SPARK_CHECK_AUDIO` (env) | unset | *Primus:* `1` checks that the audio feature count equals the audio token count on GPU inputs too (one device sync per step). CPU inputs are always checked. An environment variable, not a YAML key. |
+| `make_vocab_size_divisible_by` | (not read) | *Primus:* For Muse Spark the embedding / output rows are `vocab_size` rounded up to a multiple of 64 at every TP (202048 for the released model), the native converter's rule; the `muse_spark_vocab` patch sets `padded_vocab_size` that way and does not read this key (the module default 128 would not match the converted checkpoint). Set `padded_vocab_size` for other rows. |
+| `te_gemm_workspace_mb` | `512` | *Primus:* ROCm only. Lower bound (MiB) for each TE hipBLASLt GEMM workspace buffer: TE uses `max(TE default, this value)`. This avoids `HIPBLASLT Error: 6` for split-K GEMMs. The cost is about `size x (1 + number of GEMM streams)` per GPU. Unset or empty uses 512. Integral floats and strings are accepted (`512.0`, `"5e2"`). Any other value (e.g. `0`, `1.5`, `abc`, a bool) stops the run with a `ValueError`. |
+
+### 11.6 Native HF checkpoint conversion (`sft_trainer` / `post_trainer`)
+
+The Megatron post-training hook `runner/helpers/hooks/train/posttrain/megatron/01_convert_checkpoints.py` reads these keys from the `sft_trainer` / `post_trainer` module overrides (not `pre_trainer`). They apply to every model family with a native converter (Qwen3, DeepSeek, Llama, Muse Spark).
+
+| Parameter | Default | Description |
+|-----------|---------|-------------|
+| `native_ckpt_convert` | unset | *Primus:* `true` runs the native (bridge-free) HF to Megatron converter. `false` forces Megatron-Bridge. Unset: native for Qwen3 / DeepSeek / Llama / Muse Spark. For Muse Spark `false` is an error (Megatron-Bridge has no Muse Spark model). Accepted: a bool, `true`/`yes`/`on` / `false`/`no`/`off` (any case), and the number 1 / 0 (also `"1"`, `"1.0"`, `"0"`, `"0.0"`). An empty string means unset. Any other value (e.g. `2`, `1.5`, `y`, `enabled`) stops the hook with an error. |
+| `native_ckpt_dtype` | from the HF `torch_dtype` (else `bf16`) | *Primus:* The saved dtype of the native converter: `bf16`, `fp16` or `fp32`. The Muse Spark converter stops on any other value. |
+| `native_ckpt_max_params` | `60000000000` (60B) | *Primus:* Muse Spark converter only. The largest estimated parameter count that the single-process converter accepts. The converter builds the model with TP=PP=EP=1 and saves a `torch_dist` checkpoint; Megatron reshards it on load, so a run with any TP / PP / EP loads it. The full 816B model is above the limit (the single process holds it in host RAM), so it has no converter route. Accepts a positive integer (a string may use `_` separators or an integral float such as `60e9`). The conversion hook checks the value on every rank before any conversion starts; another value stops it with an error. For the released Hub id (`meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B`, ~816B) the hook stops at once, before any download, and asks for a converted `pretrained_checkpoint`. |
+
+The HF source is `hf_path`, else `tokenizer_model`: a local HF directory or a Hugging Face Hub id (`org/name`). A Hub id is matched only to the families without a Megatron-Bridge model (Muse Spark). Every node routes on its own, so the decision must not depend on one node's HF cache. With `native_ckpt_convert` unset, only the exact released id (`meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B`) matches; the routing reads neither the HF cache nor the network, and there is no repo-name substring match. For a fine-tuned or renamed Muse Spark repo, set `native_ckpt_convert: true`: then the Hub id's own `config.json` decides (from the HF cache, else downloaded), so every node reads the same file. For those families `native_ckpt_convert: false` stays an error, and the native converter uses the snapshot in the HF cache (downloaded when missing; the Muse Spark size cap is checked on the config before the weights are downloaded). Other Hub ids keep the Megatron-Bridge path.
+
+**Environment variables (not YAML keys).** The hook reads these from the environment of each node. A YAML key of the same name is ignored.
+
+| Variable | Default | Description |
+|----------|---------|-------------|
+| `PRIMUS_CKPT_CONVERT_TIMEOUT` | `14400` (4 h) | The longest time that the other nodes wait for rank 0's conversion while rank 0 is alive. The same for every family: a dead rank 0 is found by `PRIMUS_CKPT_CONVERT_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT`, not by this value. When no lock file appears for 600 s, the nodes stop (rank 0 did not start). A finite number > 0. |
+| `PRIMUS_CKPT_CONVERT_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT` | `300` | Rank 0 touches `<checkpoint>.converting.lock` every 30 s while it converts. When the lock file has not changed for this many seconds (measured on the waiting node's own clock), the waiting nodes stop with an error: rank 0 was killed (SIGKILL, out of memory) and could not write a `.failed` marker. Remove the stale lock file before you relaunch. A finite number > 30. |
+| `PRIMUS_CKPT_CONVERT_RUN_ID` | `$SLURM_JOB_ID` + `$SLURM_STEP_ID` (+ `$SLURM_RESTART_COUNT`), else `$MASTER_ADDR:$MASTER_PORT` | A token that is the same on every node of one launch. Rank 0 writes it into `<checkpoint>.done` and, when the conversion fails, into `<checkpoint>.failed`. A `.failed` marker written *during* a node's wait stops that node at once. A marker (`.done` or `.failed`) with another launch's token is never this run's, also when it appears during the wait: it neither stops the node nor lets it go on. A marker that was already there when the node started to wait stops it only when no lock file is there now and none has been there for `PRIMUS_CKPT_CONVERT_MARKER_GRACE` seconds, also when its token matches: an explicit run id that you keep constant, and the `$MASTER_ADDR:$MASTER_PORT` fallback (torchrun / k8s, default port 29500), are the same on a relaunch, so a matching token does not prove the marker is new. A `.done` that was there before the wait only counts when the checkpoint is complete and no lock file is present. |
+| `PRIMUS_CKPT_CONVERT_MARKER_GRACE` | `120` | See `PRIMUS_CKPT_CONVERT_RUN_ID`. A finite number > 0; every rank checks it before any conversion starts. If rank 0 starts more than this many seconds after the other nodes, a marker left by an earlier failed launch can stop them; raise the value in that case. |
+
+**Muse Spark at full size.** The native converter runs in one process (it builds with TP=PP=EP=1 and saves `torch_dist`, which Megatron reshards on load) and is capped by `native_ckpt_max_params` (60B), because it holds the whole model in host RAM. For the 816B model the default flow (the Hub id with no `pretrained_checkpoint`) therefore stops up front with an error that lists the routes. Primus ships no distributed converter. The supported routes are:
+
+1. On a host with enough RAM (about 4 bytes per parameter, ~3.3 TB for 816B), set `native_ckpt_max_params: 816000000000` (or higher). The hook then converts as for any other model. This is the one in-repo route from the HF weights.
+2. Set `pretrained_checkpoint` to a Megatron `torch_dist` checkpoint made elsewhere (any TP / PP / EP). The hook then skips conversion.
+3. Point `hf_path` / `tokenizer_model` at a smaller checkpoint, such as the 4-layer proxy (~58B), which converts with the default cap.
+
+
 ---
 
 ## 12. Reinforcement learning and GRPO-related settings

+work_group: ${PRIMUS_TEAM:amd}
+user_name: ${PRIMUS_USER:root}
+exp_name: ${PRIMUS_EXP_NAME:muse_spark_816B_A42B-pretrain}
+workspace: ${PRIMUS_WORKSPACE:./output}
+
+# Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B (text decoder, 62 layers, 256 experts top-8) BF16
+# pretraining on MI300X (192 GB = ~179 GiB per GPU). This file trains the FULL model; it
+# does not cut depth.
+#
+# Memory: 816B params x 18 bytes (bf16 weight 2 + fp32 main grad 4 + fp32 master 4 +
+# Adam exp_avg / exp_avg_sq 8) = ~14.7 TB of model states before activations. The
+# distributed optimizer shards only the 12 optimizer bytes: the dense ones over data
+# parallel (DP x CP = GPUs / (TP x PP)), the expert ones over the expert data parallel
+# group (GPUs / (EP x expert TP x PP)), which is 1 in the default layouts below, so the
+# expert optimizer bytes are not sharded there. The 6 bytes of weight + grad are only
+# split by TP x PP (dense) or EP x PP (experts) (FSDP would shard them too).
+#
+# Defaults: 32 nodes (256 GPUs), TP 1, PP 2 (31 layers per stage), EP 128 (2 experts
+# per GPU), DP 128, GBS 512 (4 micro-batches of 1 per DP rank), full recompute.
+# Model states are ~112 GiB per GPU (the memory-check estimate), so ~65 GiB are left for
+# activations. 16 nodes with TP1 / PP2 / EP64 does NOT fit here: its states alone are
+# ~165 GiB of ~179 GiB. On 16 nodes use PRIMUS_TP=8 PRIMUS_PP=2 PRIMUS_EP=64 GBS=128

+This file imports only the standard library and ``primus.core.utils.number_utils``

+Megatron) so that a bad value stops every rank before any converter runs, with the

+# this the host RAM need is in the TB range (the released 816B model): refuse it.
+MAX_PARAMS_KEY = "native_ckpt_max_params"  # sft_trainer / post_trainer config key (hook option)
+DEFAULT_MAX_PARAMS = 60 * 10**9
+
+
+def parse_max_params(value) -> int:
+    """The conversion cap from the ``native_ckpt_max_params`` config value.
+
+    None or empty -> ``DEFAULT_MAX_PARAMS``. A positive integer count; a string may use ``_``
+    separators, surrounding spaces and an integral float form (``60e9``). Anything else
+    (a bool, a fraction, NaN, <= 0) raises a ValueError that names the key.
+    """
+    return parse_positive_int(
+        value,
+        DEFAULT_MAX_PARAMS,
+        f"{MAX_PARAMS_KEY}={value!r} is not a positive integer parameter count (e.g. 60000000000 or 60e9)",
+    )

+###############################################################################
+# Copyright (c) 2026, Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. All rights reserved.
+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+###############################################################################
+
+"""Template for the Primus native (bridge-free) HF -> Megatron converters.
+
+:meth:`NativeConverter.convert` fixes the steps every converter takes; a family
+subclass fills in the model-specific ones:
+
+1. read ``config.json`` (:func:`native_convert_common.read_hf_config`);
+2. derive the Megatron fields from it (:meth:`derive_fields`, abstract) and build the
+   Megatron args (:meth:`build_margs`, abstract);
+3. initialise a single-rank Megatron and build the mcore model with the Primus model
+   provider (:meth:`build_model`; default: the ``gpt`` provider);
+4. map the HF tensors onto the model's state dict (:meth:`build_state_dict`, abstract);
+5. check the mapping is exact: no unexpected or missing model keys, no unconsumed HF
+   tensors (:func:`native_convert_common.check_exact_mapping`);
+6. save a ``torch_dist`` checkpoint from this single process (:func:`save_torch_dist`).
+   A torch_dist checkpoint carries global tensor shapes and offsets, so Megatron
+   reshards it on load: the converted TP=PP=EP=1 checkpoint loads into a run with any
+   TP / PP / EP.
+
+The llama / qwen3 / deepseek converters keep their own ``convert`` functions (legacy
+``torch`` checkpoints); new families subclass this.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import shutil
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+from primus.backends.megatron.checkpoint import native_convert_common as common
+
+
+def save_torch_dist(model, margs, save_dir, log=print):
+    """Save ``model`` as a torch_dist checkpoint (iteration ``margs.iteration``), no optimizer.
+
+    Runs in the single conversion process; the files hold global shapes and offsets, so
+    Megatron reshards them for the training layout on load. ``latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt``
+    is written as for a training save (the hook's skip-if-exists check reads it).
+    """
+    from megatron.training.checkpointing import save_checkpoint
+
+    margs.ckpt_format = "torch_dist"
+    margs.use_dist_ckpt = True
+    margs.async_save = False
+    margs.save = save_dir
+    margs.no_save_optim = True
+    margs.no_save_rng = True
+    margs.ckpt_fully_parallel_save = False
+    os.makedirs(save_dir, exist_ok=True)
+    log(f"saving torch_dist checkpoint to {save_dir} ...")
+    save_checkpoint(margs.iteration, [model], None, None, num_floating_point_operations_so_far=0)
+    log(f"DONE. Converted checkpoint at: {save_dir}")
+
+
+def existing_entries(save_dir):
+    """The names in ``save_dir`` before a save (None when it does not exist): the
+    ``existed`` argument of :func:`remove_partial_checkpoint`."""
+    return set(os.listdir(save_dir)) if os.path.isdir(save_dir) else None

+def remove_partial_checkpoint(save_dir, existed, log=print) -> None:
+    """After a failed save: drop what the save wrote, so no partial checkpoint (with a
+    ``latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt`` that the hook's skip-if-exists check reads) stays.
+
+    A directory this run created (``existed`` None / False) is removed whole. A directory
+    that was already there -- even an empty one (``existed == set()``: a ``mkdir``-ed output
+    dir or a mount point) -- is kept: the tracker is removed, and so are the entries the
+    save added (``existed`` is the set of names before it, :func:`existing_entries`), e.g. a
+    new ``iter_*`` dir of partial shards; the earlier entries may be the user's and stay
+    (``existed=True``: only the tracker).
+    """
+    if not os.path.exists(save_dir):
+        return
+    # the tracker first, on its own and checked: it is what makes a checkpoint look complete
+    tracker = os.path.join(save_dir, "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")
+    try:
+        if os.path.lexists(tracker):
+            os.remove(tracker)
+    except OSError as e:
+        log(
+            f"conversion failed and the tracker {tracker} could not be removed ({e}): delete it "
+            f"(or {save_dir}) before a relaunch, or the incomplete checkpoint is taken as complete"
+        )
+        return
+    if existed is not None and existed is not False:  # an empty set is a pre-existing dir
+        added = sorted(set(os.listdir(save_dir)) - existed) if isinstance(existed, (set, frozenset)) else []
+        errors = []
+        for name in added:
+            path = os.path.join(save_dir, name)
+            try:
+                if os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path):
+                    shutil.rmtree(path)
+                else:
+                    os.remove(path)
+            except OSError as e:
+                errors.append(f"{path}: {e}")
+        kept = f"; could not remove {len(errors)}: {errors[0]}" if errors else ""
+        n = len(added) - len(errors)
+        log(
+            f"conversion failed: removed {tracker} and the {n} new "
+            f"entr{'y' if n == 1 else 'ies'} the save wrote in {save_dir}{kept} "
+            "(entries that were there before are kept; the checkpoint is incomplete)"
+        )
+        return
+    errors = []
+    shutil.rmtree(save_dir, onerror=lambda _f, path, exc: errors.append(f"{path}: {exc[1]}"))
+    if errors or os.path.exists(save_dir):
+        log(
+            f"conversion failed: removed the tracker {tracker}, but not all of the partial "
+            f"checkpoint {save_dir} ({len(errors)} error(s), first: {errors[0] if errors else '?'}); "
+            "it has no tracker, so it is not taken as complete"
+        )
+    else:
+        log(f"conversion failed: removed the partial checkpoint {save_dir}")

+    # ---- abstract steps -------------------------------------------------------------
+    def derive_fields(self, cfg: dict) -> dict:

+        common.ensure_megatron_on_path()
+        args = SimpleNamespace(

+            save_dir=save_dir,
+            dtype=dtype,
+            tensor_parallel_size=tensor_parallel_size,
+            pipeline_parallel_size=pipeline_parallel_size,
+            expert_parallel_size=expert_parallel_size,
+            seq_length=seq_length,

+        cfg = common.read_hf_config(hf_dir)  # 1
+        fields = self.derive_fields(cfg)  # 2
+        self.check_config(fields, args, cfg)
+        margs = self.build_margs(fields, args, cfg)

+        common.assert_bridge_free("native conversion")

+        try:

+            common.assert_bridge_free("native conversion (save)")
+        except BaseException:
+            remove_partial_checkpoint(save_dir, existed, self.log)

+def build_model(margs):
+    """Build :class:`MuseSparkModel` through the ``muse_spark`` model provider."""
+    from primus.core.utils.import_utils import get_model_provider
+
+    model_provider = get_model_provider(model_type="muse_spark")
+    model = model_provider(pre_process=True, post_process=True)
+    model = model.to(margs.params_dtype)
+    # .to(dtype) casts every param; the router weight and the residual gates stay fp32
+    # (MuseSparkTopKRouter._apply restores the router; the gates restore themselves too).
+    return model
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# HF -> mcore weight mapping
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+def build_mcore_state_dict(model, store, margs, cfg_fields, log):
+    dtype = margs.params_dtype
+    padded_vocab = model.embedding.word_embeddings.weight.shape[0]
+    nh, ng, hd, hidden = (
+        margs.num_attention_heads,
+        margs.num_query_groups,
+        margs.kv_channels,
+        margs.hidden_size,
+    )
+    if nh % ng:
+        raise ValueError(f"num_attention_heads={nh} is not a multiple of num_query_groups={ng}")
+    num_experts = cfg_fields["num_experts"]
+    style = _detect_expert_key_style(model, margs.num_layers)  # the qwen3 loader's detector
+    if style is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("could not detect the MoE expert key layout on the built model")
+
+    prefix = getattr(store, "prefix", None) or detect_hf_prefix(store.all_keys())
+    if style == "grouped":
+        fc1_key, fc2_key = "{p}mlp.experts.linear_fc1.weight{e}", "{p}mlp.experts.linear_fc2.weight{e}"
+    else:
+        fc1_key = "{p}mlp.experts.local_experts.{e}.linear_fc1.weight"
+        fc2_key = "{p}mlp.experts.local_experts.{e}.linear_fc2.weight"
+    sd, consumed = {}, set()
+    q_rows = (nh // ng) * hd  # query (and output-gate) rows per KV group
+
+    def get(name, keep_fp32=False):
+        consumed.add(name)
+        return store.get(name, torch.float32 if keep_fp32 else dtype)
+
+    def gated_qkv(h):
+        q = get(h + "self_attn.q_proj.weight").reshape(ng, q_rows, hidden)
+        g = get(h + "self_attn.gate_proj.weight").reshape(ng, q_rows, hidden)
+        k = get(h + "self_attn.k_proj.weight").reshape(ng, hd, hidden)
+        v = get(h + "self_attn.v_proj.weight").reshape(ng, hd, hidden)
+        return torch.cat([q, g, k, v], dim=1).reshape(-1, hidden).contiguous()
+
+    sd["embedding.word_embeddings.weight"] = common.pad_vocab(
+        get(prefix + "embed_tokens.weight"), padded_vocab
+    )
+    sd["decoder.final_layernorm.weight"] = get(prefix + "norm.weight")
+    if margs.untie_embeddings_and_output_weights:
+        sd["output_layer.weight"] = common.pad_vocab(get("lm_head.weight"), padded_vocab)
+
+    for L in range(margs.num_layers):
+        p = f"decoder.layers.{L}."
+        h = f"{prefix}layers.{L}."
+        sd[p + "input_layernorm.weight"] = get(h + "input_layernorm.weight")
+        sd[p + "self_attention.linear_qkv.weight"] = gated_qkv(h)
+        sd[p + "self_attention.linear_proj.weight"] = get(h + "self_attn.o_proj.weight")
+        sd[p + "self_attn_bda.gate"] = get(h + "post_attention_residual_gate.gate", keep_fp32=True)
+        sd[p + "pre_mlp_layernorm.weight"] = get(h + "pre_feedforward_layernorm.weight")
+        sd[p + "mlp.router.weight"] = get(h + "mlp.gate.weight", keep_fp32=True)
+        sd[p + "mlp.router.expert_bias"] = get(h + "mlp.gate.e_score_correction_bias", keep_fp32=True)
+        sd[p + "mlp.fc1_latent_proj.weight"] = get(h + "mlp.pre_expert_proj.weight")
+        sd[p + "mlp.pre_expert_norm.weight"] = get(h + "mlp.pre_expert_norm.weight")
+        sd[p + "mlp.post_expert_norm.weight"] = get(h + "mlp.experts.post_expert_norm.weight")
+        sd[p + "mlp.fc2_latent_proj.weight"] = get(h + "mlp.post_expert_proj.weight")
+        sd[p + "mlp_bda.post_norm.weight"] = get(h + "post_feedforward_layernorm.weight")
+        sd[p + "mlp_bda.gate"] = get(h + "post_feedforward_residual_gate.gate", keep_fp32=True)
+
+        gate_up = get(h + "mlp.experts.gate_up_proj")  # [E, 2I, latent]: [gate; up]
+        down = get(h + "mlp.experts.down_proj")  # [E, latent, I]
+        if gate_up.shape[0] != num_experts or down.shape[0] != num_experts:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{h}mlp.experts: gate_up_proj / down_proj have {gate_up.shape[0]} / {down.shape[0]} "
+                f"experts, the config has {num_experts}"
+            )
+        for e in range(num_experts):
+            sd[fc1_key.format(p=p, e=e)] = gate_up[e].contiguous()
+            sd[fc2_key.format(p=p, e=e)] = down[e].contiguous()
+        del gate_up, down
+        log(f"layer {L} mapped ({style} experts)")
+
+    if getattr(model, "audio_tower", None) is not None:
+        sd.update(map_audio_tower(model.audio_tower, audio_prefix(prefix), get, log))
+    return sd, consumed
+
+
+def audio_prefix(text_prefix):
+    """The HF audio-tower prefix next to the text prefix (``model.audio_tower.``)."""
+    return (
+        text_prefix.replace("language_model.", "audio_tower.", 1)
+        if "language_model." in text_prefix
+        else None
+    )
+
+
+def map_audio_tower(tower, prefix, get, log=print):
+    """HF ``<prefix>*`` -> ``audio_tower.*``: the module names are the same (one to one)."""
+    if not prefix:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "the model has an audio_tower, but the checkpoint is text-only (no audio tower prefix)"
+        )
+    out = {}
+    for name in tower.state_dict():
+        out["audio_tower." + name] = get(prefix + name)
+    log(f"audio tower mapped: {len(out)} tensors from {prefix}*")
+    return out
+
+
+def detect_hf_prefix(keys):
+    """The text-decoder key prefix of an HF Muse Spark checkpoint (one of ``HF_PREFIXES``),
+    found from ``<prefix>embed_tokens.weight``; raise on an unknown layout."""
+    keys = set(keys)
+    for prefix in HF_PREFIXES:
+        if f"{prefix}embed_tokens.weight" in keys:
+            return prefix
+    found = sorted({k.split(".", 1)[0] + "." for k in keys if "." in k})
+    found += sorted({k[: k.index("embed_tokens.")] or "<none>" for k in keys if "embed_tokens." in k})
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"unsupported Muse Spark checkpoint layout: no embed_tokens.weight under any of {HF_PREFIXES}; "
+        f"found key prefixes {found}"
+    )
+
+
+def is_text_key(name, prefix=HF_PREFIX):
+    """True for the text decoder's HF tensors (the ones this converter maps)."""
+    return name.startswith(prefix) or name.startswith("lm_head.")
+
+
+class MappedStore:
+    """A SafetensorsStore view whose ``all_keys`` holds only the tensors this port maps:
+    the text decoder and (``with_audio``) the audio tower; not the vision tower.
+
+    The exact-mapping check fails on HF tensors the mapping did not consume; the vision
+    tower and its adapter are not ported yet (and the audio tower is not mapped when the
+    built model has none), so those are logged and excluded from it.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, store, log=print, with_audio=True):
+        self._store = store
+        keys = store.all_keys()
+        self.prefix = detect_hf_prefix(keys)
+        audio = audio_prefix(self.prefix) if with_audio else None  # computed once, not per key
+        self._mapped_keys = frozenset(
+            k for k in keys if is_text_key(k, self.prefix) or (audio is not None and k.startswith(audio))
+        )
+        self.skipped = sorted(k for k in keys if k not in self._mapped_keys)
+        if self.skipped:
+            scope = "vision" if with_audio else "vision + audio"
+            log(
+                f"not mapped (out of scope: {scope} tower): {len(self.skipped)} tensors, e.g. {self.skipped[:4]}"
+            )
+
+    def all_keys(self):
+        # the key set is fixed: computed once in __init__ (a fresh set, callers may mutate it)
+        return set(self._mapped_keys)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name):
+        return getattr(self._store, name)
+
+
+class MuseSparkConverter(NativeConverter):
+    """The Muse Spark text decoder on the :class:`NativeConverter` template.
+
+    Single-rank build (TP = PP = EP = 1) with grouped-GEMM experts and the training vocab
+    padding; saved as torch_dist, so a run with any TP / PP / EP loads it (Megatron
+    reshards on load).
+    """
+
+    family = "muse-spark"
+    with_audio = True  # set from the built model in check_model
+
+    def derive_fields(self, cfg):
+        return derive_megatron_fields(cfg)
+
+    def check_config(self, fields, args, cfg):
+        check_convert_size(fields, cfg, max_params=getattr(args, "max_params", None))
+
+    def build_margs(self, fields, args, cfg):
+        return build_margs(fields, args, cfg)
+
+    def build_model(self, margs):
+        return build_model(margs)
+
+    def check_model(self, model, margs):
+        # Checked on the model, not on the mapped dict (that one is fp32 by construction):
+        # load_state_dict keeps the model's dtypes, so these are the saved dtypes.
+        check_fp32_tensors(model.state_dict(), margs.num_layers)
+        self.with_audio = getattr(model, "audio_tower", None) is not None
+
+    def open_store(self, hf_dir):
+        return MappedStore(common.SafetensorsStore(hf_dir), self.log, with_audio=self.with_audio)
+
+    def build_state_dict(self, model, store, margs, fields):
+        return build_mcore_state_dict(model, store, margs, fields, self.log)
+
+
+def convert(
+    hf_dir,
+    save_dir,
+    *,
+    dtype="bf16",
+    tensor_parallel_size=1,
+    pipeline_parallel_size=1,
+    expert_parallel_size=1,
+    seq_length=4096,
+    make_vocab_size_divisible_by=MAKE_VOCAB_SIZE_DIVISIBLE_BY,
+    master_port=None,

+    """Full conversion (the posttrain conversion hook calls this): build, map, check the
+    mapping is exact, save a torch_dist checkpoint. ``max_params`` is the
+    ``native_ckpt_max_params`` config value (None -> 60B). ``master_port`` None uses
+    ``NativeConverter.master_port``."""
+    return MuseSparkConverter(log=log).convert(
+        hf_dir,
+        save_dir,
+        dtype=dtype,
+        tensor_parallel_size=tensor_parallel_size,
+        pipeline_parallel_size=pipeline_parallel_size,

+"""Causal attention (query, key) pair counts for FLOPs accounting.
+
+Pure Python (no torch / Megatron). Used by the Muse Spark and DeepSeek-V4 FLOPs patches (one formula for both).
+"""
+
+__all__ = ["causal_visible_pairs"]
+
+
+def causal_visible_pairs(seq_length: int, window=None) -> int:
+    """Number of (query, key) pairs that causal attention computes over ``seq_length``
+    tokens when each query sees at most ``window`` keys (itself included).
+
+    ``window`` is an int key count (HF ``sliding_window``, the query included). None, <= 0
+    (the callers' "no window", as in DeepSeek-V4's ``swa_window``) or >= ``seq_length``
+    means full causal attention: ``S * (S + 1) / 2``. Otherwise queries ``0 .. W-1`` see
+    ``q + 1`` keys and the rest see ``W``: ``W * S - W * (W - 1) / 2``. A Megatron
+    ``window_size`` tuple ``(left, right)`` is not a key count: convert it first
+    (``left + 1`` for ``right == 0``); it raises TypeError here.
+    """
+    if isinstance(window, (tuple, list)):
+        raise TypeError(
+            f"window must be an int key count, got {window!r}; for a Megatron window_size "
+            "(left, 0) pass left + 1"
+        )
+    s = int(seq_length)
+    w = int(window or 0)
+    if w <= 0 or w >= s:
+        return s * (s + 1) // 2
+    return w * s - w * (w - 1) // 2

+    the model kwargs.
+
+    No module opts in -> a no-op: nothing is checked or split, and the caller's
+    ``fully_shard`` is the only sharding applied.
+
+    An island's dtype is that of its direct *trainable* parameters; when it has any,
+    its frozen direct parameters do not decide (or have to match) the dtype. A fully

+    parameters share one dtype; with mixed frozen dtypes it is left to the parent

+#
+# See LICENSE for license information.
+###############################################################################
+
+"""Enlarge Transformer Engine's GEMM workspace (ROCm hipBLASLt split-K needs more than the default).
+
+The one implementation of this ROCm workaround. Users:
+
+* Muse Spark (``before_train``), through ``apply_rocm_te_gemm_workspace``, which raises
+  on ROCm when nothing is patched. The size is the ``te_gemm_workspace_mb`` arg (512
+  when unset) or an explicit ``mb``; both go through ``parse_workspace_mb``, so a value
+  that is not a positive integer stops the run.
+* GLM-5.3 (``glm5_next_patches``), through ``apply_rocm_te_gemm_workspace`` too, with
+  ``required=False`` (best effort: logs a warning when nothing is patched and keeps TE's
+  workspace) and the size from ``PRIMUS_TE_GEMM_WORKSPACE_MB`` (parsed by
+  ``workspace_mb_from_env``: unset is 512, blank raises, an integer <= 0 is no change;
+  ROCm only).
+
+``enlarge_te_gemm_workspace`` is idempotent: a second call with the same or a smaller
+size changes nothing.
+
+TE builds keep the workspace size function, ``get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes``, in
+different modules (``module.base`` in the TE of the Primus image; older builds use
+``cpp_extensions.gemm``), and other TE modules may hold their own reference to it
+(``from .base import get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes``). So the helper:
+
+* imports the known modules, then visits every loaded ``transformer_engine.*`` module
+  that has a ``get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes`` attribute and rebinds it;
+* drops the cached workspaces in those modules: the ``lru_cache`` of
+  ``get_cublas_workspace`` / ``get_workspace`` / ``get_multi_stream_cublas_workspace``,
+  and the module globals ``_cublas_workspace`` / ``_multi_stream_cublas_workspace``,
+  so the next GEMM allocates the larger buffer.
+
+A reference captured in a closure or a default argument cannot be reached; no TE
+version known to us does that. Only ``transformer_engine.*`` modules are scanned:
+Primus's own ``primus.backends.transformer_engine.pytorch.module.base`` defines a
+``get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes`` that returns 0, but it belongs to the Primus
+``torch.mm`` GEMM path (no hipBLASLt workspace) and TE never calls it, so there is
+nothing to enlarge there. ``enlarge_te_gemm_workspace`` is best effort and reports
+errors and notes in its result; ``apply_rocm_te_gemm_workspace`` (``required=True``,
+Muse Spark) raises on ROCm when nothing could be patched (fail fast instead of
+"HIPBLASLT Error: 6" later).
+
+Memory: the size is a lower bound per workspace buffer. TE allocates one buffer for
+the default stream and, for grouped / multi-stream GEMMs, one per extra stream
+(``get_multi_stream_cublas_workspace``), so the per-GPU cost is about
+``size x (1 + number of GEMM streams)``, e.g. ~2.5 GiB at 512 MiB and 4 streams.
+Lower the ``te_gemm_workspace_mb`` config / args value to trade memory for split-K headroom.
+"""
+
+import contextlib
+import importlib
+import os
+import sys
+
+from primus.core.utils.module_utils import log_rank_0, warning_rank_0
+from primus.core.utils.number_utils import parse_positive_int
+
+__all__ = [
+    "enlarge_te_gemm_workspace",
+    "apply_rocm_te_gemm_workspace",
+    "workspace_mb_of",
+    "parse_workspace_mb",
+    "DEFAULT_MB",
+    "ARG_MB",
+]
+
+ARG_MB = "te_gemm_workspace_mb"  # config / args key (muse_spark_base.yaml: 512)
+DEFAULT_MB = 512
+SIZE_FN = "get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes"
+_KNOWN = (
+    "transformer_engine.pytorch.module.base",
+    "transformer_engine.pytorch.cpp_extensions.gemm",
+)
+_CACHED_FUNCS = ("get_cublas_workspace", "get_workspace", "get_multi_stream_cublas_workspace")
+_CACHE_GLOBALS = ("_cublas_workspace", "_multi_stream_cublas_workspace")
+
+
+def _size_fn(original, size_bytes):
+    """``max(original(), size_bytes)``, evaluated per call, so TE's own size is kept when
+    it is larger. When ``original()`` raises (TE's size is unknown, e.g. "No HIP GPUs are
+    available" before the device is set), the call returns ``size_bytes``.
+
+    Evaluating ``original`` on each call, not once at patch time, avoids guessing. The
+    first such error is logged (once), so a broken TE size function is not hidden.
+    """
+    logged = []
+
+    def get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes() -> int:
+        try:
+            return max(int(original()), size_bytes)
+        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - TE's size still unknown: use ours
+            if not logged:
+                logged.append(e)
+                warning_rank_0(
+                    f"[te_gemm_workspace] TE's {SIZE_FN}() raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}; using "
+                    f"the Primus size {size_bytes} bytes (logged once)"
+                )
+            return size_bytes
+
+    get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes._primus_workspace_bytes = size_bytes
+    get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes._primus_original = original
+    return get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes
+
+
+def _drop_caches(mod):
+    for fn in _CACHED_FUNCS:
+        cache_clear = getattr(getattr(mod, fn, None), "cache_clear", None)
+        if cache_clear is not None:
+            cache_clear()
+    for g in _CACHE_GLOBALS:
+        cur = getattr(mod, g, None)
+        if isinstance(cur, (list, dict)):
+            cur.clear()
+        elif cur is not None:
+            setattr(mod, g, None)
+
+
+def enlarge_te_gemm_workspace(size_bytes: int):
+    """Make every TE ``get_cublas_workspace_size_bytes`` report ``max(TE's size, size_bytes)``.
+
+    Returns ``(enlarged, unchanged, errors, notes)``:
+
+    * ``enlarged``: modules whose size function now returns at least ``size_bytes``
+      (rebound to a ``max`` wrapper, cached workspaces dropped);
+    * ``unchanged``: modules whose TE size already is >= ``size_bytes`` (or that were
+      already patched to at least that size); nothing done;
+    * ``errors``: ``"module: error"`` strings for real failures (a failed rebind, a
+      broken import, or a missing known module when nothing was patched);
+    * ``notes``: informational ``"module: ..."`` strings that do not need action: a
+      size probe that raised (the module was still patched; the wrapper asks TE
+      again on each call), or a known module that does not exist in this TE build
+      (``ImportError``) while another module was patched.
+
+    Best effort: this function does not raise.
+    """
+    errors, notes, missing = [], [], []
+    for name in _KNOWN:
+        try:
+            importlib.import_module(name)
+        except ImportError as e:  # this TE build does not have the module (or no TE at all)
+            missing.append(f"{name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
+        except Exception as e:  # broken extension (OSError), no GPU, ...
+            errors.append(f"{name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
+    enlarged, unchanged = [], []
+    for name, mod in sorted(sys.modules.items()):
+        if mod is None or not (name == "transformer_engine" or name.startswith("transformer_engine.")):
+            continue
+        try:
+            get_size = mod.__dict__.get(SIZE_FN)
+            if get_size is None:
+                continue
+            already = getattr(get_size, "_primus_workspace_bytes", None)
+            if already is not None and already >= size_bytes:
+                unchanged.append(name)
+                continue
+            original = getattr(get_size, "_primus_original", get_size)
+            try:
+                current = int(original())
+            except Exception as e:  # e.g. "No HIP GPUs are available"
+                notes.append(f"{name}: size probe failed ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); patched with max()")
+                current = None
+            if current is not None and current >= size_bytes:
+                unchanged.append(name)
+                continue
+            setattr(mod, SIZE_FN, _size_fn(original, size_bytes))
+            _drop_caches(mod)
+            enlarged.append(name)
+        except Exception as e:
+            errors.append(f"{name}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
+    (notes if enlarged or unchanged else errors).extend(missing)
+    return enlarged, unchanged, errors, notes
+
+
+def parse_workspace_mb(raw, name: str = ARG_MB) -> int:
+    """``raw`` as a positive int (MiB); ``name`` is used in the error.
+
+    DEFAULT_MB when unset (None or an empty string). Accepted: an int (also a numpy
+    integer), an integral float (``512.0``) and a string of either (``"512"``, ``"512.0"``,
+    ``"5e2"``). Anything else (a bool, a fraction, NaN / inf, <= 0, an unparsable string)
+    raises ValueError: a typo must not silently run with another workspace size.
+    """
+    return parse_positive_int(
+        raw, DEFAULT_MB, f"{name}={raw!r} is not a positive integer number of MiB (e.g. 512)"
+    )
+
+
+def workspace_mb_from_env(env_name: str, environ=None):
+    """The workspace size (MiB) set by the environment variable ``env_name``, for a caller
+    configured by env (GLM-5.3); None when the value is an integer <= 0 ("no enlargement",
+    e.g. ``0`` or ``-1``).
+
+    Unset is DEFAULT_MB. Every other value goes through :func:`parse_workspace_mb`, the
+    parser of the ``te_gemm_workspace_mb`` arg, so the env and the YAML key accept the same
+    sizes: a blank value, a non-integer (``-0.5``, ``0.5``), ``-inf`` / ``nan`` or text
+    raise ValueError naming ``env_name``.
+    """
+    raw = (os.environ if environ is None else environ).get(env_name)
+    if raw is None:
+        return DEFAULT_MB
+    if not raw.strip():  # set but blank is a config error: unset it for the default
+        raise ValueError(f"{env_name}={raw!r} is blank; unset it for the {DEFAULT_MB} MiB default")
+    with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):  # not an integer: parse_workspace_mb names the variable
+        if int(raw.strip()) <= 0:  # only an integer opts out ("0", "-1"); "-0.5" / "-inf" raise
+            return None
+    return parse_workspace_mb(raw, env_name)
+
+
+def workspace_mb_of(args) -> int:
+    """``args.te_gemm_workspace_mb`` through :func:`parse_workspace_mb` (512 when unset)."""
+    # ARG_MB, read as a literal so the config-schema scan sees the key in use
+    return parse_workspace_mb(getattr(args, "te_gemm_workspace_mb", None))
+
+
+def apply_rocm_te_gemm_workspace(
+    tag: str, args=None, mb=None, mb_name: str = "mb", required: bool = True
+) -> list:
+    """The ``before_train`` patch body: on ROCm, TE GEMM workspace >= ``mb`` MiB.
+
+    ``mb`` defaults to ``workspace_mb_of(args)`` (``args.te_gemm_workspace_mb``, 512); an
+    explicit ``mb`` is validated the same way (:func:`parse_workspace_mb`: 0, -5, 1.5 or
+    ``"abc"`` raise ValueError naming ``mb_name``; ``""`` is DEFAULT_MB; ``mb=None`` uses
+    ``args.te_gemm_workspace_mb``, itself DEFAULT_MB when unset). Logs errors as warnings and
+    notes as info. ``required`` (Muse Spark): raise RuntimeError on ROCm when no TE size
+    function could be found or patched, since the run would otherwise fail later with
+    "HIPBLASLT Error: 6". ``required=False`` (GLM-5.3, best effort) logs that as a
+    warning and keeps TE's own workspace. Returns
+    the enlarged modules. Off ROCm it only validates the value and returns ``[]``.
+    """
+    import torch
+
+    # parsed on every platform: a bad value fails on CUDA too, not only later on ROCm
+    mb = workspace_mb_of(args) if mb is None else parse_workspace_mb(mb, mb_name)
+    if torch.version.hip is None:
+        return []
+    size = mb * 1024 * 1024
+    enlarged, unchanged, errors, notes = enlarge_te_gemm_workspace(size)
+    if not enlarged and not unchanged:
+        msg = (
+            f"{tag} no Transformer Engine {SIZE_FN} found or patched (errors: {errors or 'none'}); "
+            "the default TE GEMM workspace is too small for hipBLASLt split-K (HIPBLASLT Error: 6)"
+        )
+        if required:
+            raise RuntimeError(msg)
+        warning_rank_0(msg + "; going on with TE's own workspace")
+        return []
+    if enlarged:
+        log_rank_0(
+            f"{tag} TE GEMM workspace -> max(TE default, {mb} MiB) in {', '.join(enlarged)} "
+            f"(per GPU: one buffer, plus one per multi-stream GEMM stream)"
+        )
+    if unchanged:
+        log_rank_0(f"{tag} TE GEMM workspace already >= {mb} MiB in {', '.join(unchanged)}")
+    for n in notes:
+        log_rank_0(f"{tag} {n}")
+    for e in errors:
+        warning_rank_0(f"{tag} {e}")
+    return enlarged

+"""Muse Spark waveform audio encoder and the audio placeholder merge.
+
+HF ``MuseSparkAudioModel`` (transformers ``modeling_muse_spark.py``): raw mono 24 kHz
+audio, no spectrogram. Four stages; stage ``i`` is
+
+* a patch embedding: ``reshape(B, T / p_i, p_i * C)`` -> ``Linear`` (bias) -> RMSNorm
+  (weight, ``eps``);
+* ``depths[i]`` conv blocks: ``x + mlp(norm(causal_depthwise_conv(x)))``, the conv with
+  kernel ``k`` and left padding ``k - 1`` (so output ``t`` sees inputs ``<= t`` only), the
+  MLP ``fc1 -> act -> fc2`` with biases and width ``mlp_ratio * hidden``.
+
+Then ``RMSNorm -> Linear(hidden[-1], out_hidden) -> RMSNorm``. One output token covers
+``prod(patch_sizes)`` samples (1920 = 80 ms).
+
+Module and parameter names follow HF, so the checkpoint maps one to one
+(``model.audio_tower.<name>`` -> ``audio_tower.<name>``).
+
+:func:`audio_features` is HF ``get_audio_features``: it drops the tokens of right padding
+(``input_values_mask``) and applies the text embedding norm (weightless RMSNorm).
+:func:`merge_audio` is the placeholder scatter of HF ``MuseSparkModel.forward``.
+"""
+
+import math
+import os
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+from torch import nn
+
+from primus.backends.megatron.core.transformer.muse_spark.norms import (
+    MuseSparkRMSNorm,
+    _rms,
+)
+
+__all__ = [
+    "AUDIO_CONFIG_KEYS",
+    "MuseSparkAudioEncoder",
+    "audio_config_from_hf",
+    "audio_features",
+    "merge_audio",
+    "samples_per_token",
+]
+
+# HF audio_config keys the encoder uses, with the HF defaults.
+AUDIO_CONFIG_KEYS = {
+    "hidden_sizes": [256, 512, 1024, 2048],
+    "depths": [2, 2, 2, 2],
+    "patch_sizes": [16, 6, 5, 4],
+    "conv_kernel_size": 7,
+    "mlp_ratio": 4.0,
+    "hidden_act": "gelu",
+    "rms_norm_eps": 1e-6,
+    "out_hidden_size": 8192,
+}
+
+_ACT = {
+    "gelu": F.gelu,
+    "gelu_new": lambda x: F.gelu(x, approximate="tanh"),
+    "gelu_pytorch_tanh": lambda x: F.gelu(x, approximate="tanh"),
+    "silu": F.silu,
+    "relu": F.relu,
+}
+
+
+def audio_config_from_hf(cfg: Optional[dict]) -> Optional[dict]:
+    """The encoder settings from an HF ``audio_config`` dict (None when there is none).
+
+    Raises on a value the encoder does not support (unknown activation, list lengths that
+    differ)."""
+    if not cfg:
+        return None
+    out = {k: cfg.get(k, v) for k, v in AUDIO_CONFIG_KEYS.items()}
+    out["hidden_sizes"] = [int(x) for x in out["hidden_sizes"]]
+    out["depths"] = [int(x) for x in out["depths"]]
+    out["patch_sizes"] = [int(x) for x in out["patch_sizes"]]
+    n = int(cfg.get("num_hidden_layers", len(out["hidden_sizes"])))
+    lens = {len(out["hidden_sizes"]), len(out["depths"]), len(out["patch_sizes"]), n}
+    if len(lens) != 1:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Muse Spark audio_config: hidden_sizes / depths / patch_sizes / num_hidden_layers "
+            f"disagree on the stage count: {out}"
+        )
+    if out["hidden_act"] not in _ACT:
+        raise ValueError(f"Muse Spark audio_config: hidden_act {out['hidden_act']!r} is not supported")
+    return out
+
+
+def samples_per_token(cfg: dict) -> int:
+    return math.prod(cfg["patch_sizes"])
+
+
+class MuseSparkAudioCausalConv1d(nn.Conv1d):
+    """Conv1d with left padding only (``(k - 1) * dilation + 1 - stride``): causal.
+
+    New math: Megatron has no causal depthwise convolution over time."""
+
+    @property
+    def left_pad(self) -> int:
+        return (self.kernel_size[0] - 1) * self.dilation[0] + 1 - self.stride[0]
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return super().forward(F.pad(x, (self.left_pad, 0)))
+
+
+class MuseSparkAudioPatchEmbedding(nn.Module):
+    """New math: Megatron has no waveform patch embedding (reshape of raw samples ->
+    Linear -> RMSNorm)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, cfg: dict, idx: int):
+        super().__init__()
+        in_ch = 1 if idx == 0 else cfg["hidden_sizes"][idx - 1]
+        out_ch = cfg["hidden_sizes"][idx]
+        self.patch_size = cfg["patch_sizes"][idx]
+        self.proj = nn.Linear(in_ch * self.patch_size, out_ch, bias=True)
+        self.norm = MuseSparkRMSNorm(hidden_size=out_ch, eps=cfg["rms_norm_eps"])
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        b, t, c = x.shape
+        if t % self.patch_size:
+            raise ValueError(f"audio length {t} is not a multiple of the patch size {self.patch_size}")
+        return self.norm(self.proj(x.reshape(b, t // self.patch_size, self.patch_size * c)))
+
+
+class MuseSparkAudioMLP(nn.Module):
+    """``fc2(act(fc1(x)))`` with biases, at the per-stage audio width (256 .. 2048).
+
+    New math: Megatron's MLP is the decoder MLP (TP-sharded, hidden_size from the
+    TransformerConfig); the audio stages have their own widths and are not tensor parallel
+    (the whole encoder is ~0.1 B params and runs replicated on the first stage)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, cfg: dict, idx: int):
+        super().__init__()
+        h = cfg["hidden_sizes"][idx]
+        inter = int(h * cfg["mlp_ratio"])
+        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(h, inter, bias=True)
+        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(inter, h, bias=True)
+        self.act = _ACT[cfg["hidden_act"]]
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.fc2(self.act(self.fc1(x)))
+
+
+class MuseSparkAudioConvBlock(nn.Module):
+    """``x + mlp(norm(causal_depthwise_conv(x)))``.
+
+    New math: a convolution block with no attention; Megatron's TransformerLayer /
+    TransformerBlock have no conv mixer."""
+
+    def __init__(self, cfg: dict, idx: int):
+        super().__init__()
+        h = cfg["hidden_sizes"][idx]
+        self.conv = MuseSparkAudioCausalConv1d(h, h, kernel_size=cfg["conv_kernel_size"], groups=h, bias=True)
+        self.norm = MuseSparkRMSNorm(hidden_size=h, eps=cfg["rms_norm_eps"])
+        self.mlp = MuseSparkAudioMLP(cfg, idx)
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        y = self.conv(x.transpose(1, 2)).transpose(1, 2)
+        return self.mlp(self.norm(y)) + x
+
+
+class MuseSparkAudioLayer(nn.Module):
+    """One encoder stage: patch embedding (downsampling) then conv blocks.
+
+    New math: a downsampling conv stage; Megatron's TransformerLayer has no such layer."""
+
+    def __init__(self, cfg: dict, idx: int):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.patch_embedder = MuseSparkAudioPatchEmbedding(cfg, idx)
+        self.conv_blocks = nn.ModuleList(MuseSparkAudioConvBlock(cfg, idx) for _ in range(cfg["depths"][idx]))
+
+    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        x = self.patch_embedder(x)
+        for block in self.conv_blocks:
+            x = block(x)
+        return x
+
+
+class MuseSparkAudioEncoder(nn.Module):
+    """``[B, samples]`` waveform -> ``[B, samples / prod(patch_sizes), out_hidden_size]``.
+
+    New math: a causal convolutional pyramid encoder (no attention, no spectrogram);
+    Megatron has no audio / conv encoder to build on. It is small (~0.1 B params), so it is
+    replicated (not tensor / pipeline parallel) and lives on the first pipeline stage."""
+
+    def __init__(self, cfg: dict):
+        super().__init__()
+        self.cfg = dict(cfg)
+        self.samples_per_token = samples_per_token(cfg)
+        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(MuseSparkAudioLayer(cfg, i) for i in range(len(cfg["hidden_sizes"])))
+        self.norm = MuseSparkRMSNorm(hidden_size=cfg["hidden_sizes"][-1], eps=cfg["rms_norm_eps"])
+        self.proj = nn.Linear(cfg["hidden_sizes"][-1], cfg["out_hidden_size"], bias=True)
+        self.post_proj_norm = MuseSparkRMSNorm(hidden_size=cfg["out_hidden_size"], eps=cfg["rms_norm_eps"])
+
+    def forward(self, input_values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if input_values.dim() != 2 or input_values.shape[1] % self.samples_per_token:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"input_values must be [batch, samples] with samples a multiple of "
+                f"{self.samples_per_token}; got {tuple(input_values.shape)}"
+            )
+        x = input_values.to(device=self.proj.weight.device, dtype=self.proj.weight.dtype).unsqueeze(-1)
+        for layer in self.layers:
+            x = layer(x)
+        return self.post_proj_norm(self.proj(self.norm(x)))
+
+
+def padded_audio_features(
+    encoder: MuseSparkAudioEncoder,
+    input_values: torch.Tensor,
+    input_values_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    embed_norm_eps: float,
+):
+    """``(feats, n_tok)``: the normed features of every token, padded ``[B, T, out_hidden]``,
+    and the real token count of each clip (``[B]`` on the features' device; None without a
+    mask: all ``T`` tokens are real). No data-dependent shape, so no device sync.
+
+    ``input_values_mask`` ``[B, samples]`` marks real samples (right padding only); a clip
+    keeps ``ceil(len / samples_per_token)`` tokens. The features pass the text embedding
+    norm (weightless RMSNorm in fp32, eps = ``embed_norm_eps``), a per-token op, so norming
+    the padded rows too changes nothing for the real ones."""
+    feats = encoder(input_values)
+    feats = _rms(feats.float(), embed_norm_eps).type_as(feats)
+    if input_values_mask is None:
+        return feats, None
+    spt = encoder.samples_per_token
+    n_tok = ((input_values_mask.sum(-1) + spt - 1) // spt).to(feats.device)
+    return feats, n_tok
+
+
+def audio_features(
+    encoder: MuseSparkAudioEncoder,
+    input_values: torch.Tensor,
+    input_values_mask: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    embed_norm_eps: float,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """HF ``get_audio_features``: ``[N, out_hidden]`` features of the real (unpadded) tokens,
+    batch-major (:func:`padded_audio_features` with the padding dropped; the boolean index
+    has a data-dependent size, a device sync: the model's forward uses
+    :func:`merge_padded_audio` instead)."""
+    feats, n_tok = padded_audio_features(encoder, input_values, input_values_mask, embed_norm_eps)
+    if n_tok is None:
+        return feats.reshape(-1, feats.shape[-1])
+    pos = torch.arange(feats.shape[1], device=feats.device)
+    return feats[pos[None, :] < n_tok[:, None]]
+
+
+def merge_padded_audio(
+    embeddings: torch.Tensor, audio_mask: torch.Tensor, feats: torch.Tensor, n_tok: Optional[torch.Tensor]
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """:func:`merge_audio` of the real rows of padded ``feats`` (``[B_a, T, H]``, from
+    :func:`padded_audio_features`) without a device sync: the k-th audio token (batch-major
+    over ``audio_mask``) takes the k-th real feature row, found on device with a cumsum
+    of ``audio_mask`` and a searchsorted over the clips' token counts."""
+    b_a, t, h = feats.shape
+    if n_tok is None:
+        n_tok = torch.full((b_a,), t, dtype=torch.long, device=feats.device)
+    n_tok = n_tok.to(device=audio_mask.device, dtype=torch.long)
+    if audio_mask.device.type == "cpu" or os.environ.get("MUSE_SPARK_CHECK_AUDIO") == "1":
+        n, have = int(audio_mask.sum()), int(n_tok.sum())
+        if n != have:
+            raise ValueError(f"Audio features and audio tokens do not match, tokens: {n}, features: {have}")
+    flat_mask = audio_mask.reshape(-1)
+    k = torch.cumsum(flat_mask.long(), 0) - 1  # index of each audio token among all of them
+    ends = torch.cumsum(n_tok, 0)  # end (exclusive) of each clip's real rows
+    clip = torch.searchsorted(ends, k.clamp(min=0), right=True).clamp(max=b_a - 1)
+    row = clip * t + (k.clamp(min=0) - (ends[clip] - n_tok[clip])).clamp(0, t - 1)
+    picked = feats.reshape(-1, h).to(embeddings.device, embeddings.dtype)[row.to(embeddings.device)]
+    bsh = embeddings.transpose(0, 1)  # [B, S, H]
+    out = torch.where(audio_mask.to(embeddings.device).unsqueeze(-1), picked.view(bsh.shape), bsh)
+    return out.transpose(0, 1).contiguous()
+
+
+def merge_audio(embeddings: torch.Tensor, audio_mask: torch.Tensor, feats: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Write ``feats`` (``[N, H]``, batch-major order) into the rows of ``embeddings``
+    (``[S, B, H]``, Megatron layout) where ``audio_mask`` (``[B, S]``) is True."""
+    # the count check reads the mask on the host (a device sync): only when the mask is on
+    # the CPU or MUSE_SPARK_CHECK_AUDIO=1; masked_scatter itself needs no count
+    if audio_mask.device.type == "cpu" or os.environ.get("MUSE_SPARK_CHECK_AUDIO") == "1":
+        n = int(audio_mask.sum())
+        if n != feats.shape[0]:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"Audio features and audio tokens do not match, tokens: {n}, features: {feats.shape[0]}"
+            )
+    out = embeddings.transpose(0, 1).masked_scatter(audio_mask.unsqueeze(-1), feats.to(embeddings.dtype))
+    return out.transpose(0, 1).contiguous()

+"""Muse Spark per-layer 0/1 patterns (``window_attn_skip_freq`` / ``no_rope_freq``).
+
+One parser for the config and the ``build_args`` patch. It reads an int, a list,
+or a Python-list expression string such as ``"([1,0,1,1]*15+[1,0])"`` without
+``eval``: only int literals (with unary minus), flat int list / tuple literals,
+``list * int``, ``int * list`` and ``list + list`` are accepted. A list may hold at
+most ``MAX_PATTERN_LEN`` entries (checked before a repetition is built), a string at
+most ``MAX_SOURCE_LEN`` characters, and every malformed input (including unary minus
+on a list and deeply nested expressions) raises ValueError. An int means "every N-th layer" (Megatron's
+meaning) and must be >= 1.
+
+A longer list is cut to ``num_layers`` on purpose: a depth-reduced build (proxy,
+trainer test) keeps the first layers of the released model, so it keeps the first
+pattern entries. The cut is reported through the ``warn`` callback (the ``build_args``
+patch logs it on rank 0), so a wrong ``num_layers`` (e.g. 60 for the 62-layer release)
+is visible in the log; the checkpoint converter derives ``num_layers`` from the HF
+config, so its patterns always match exactly. A shorter list is an error, and an int
+must be in ``[1, num_layers]`` (a larger N skips no layer). Every error names the
+argument. Pure Python (no torch / Megatron).
+"""
+
+import ast
+import re
+
+# re-exported: the one implementation lives in the shared light helper
+from primus.backends.megatron.core.attention_pairs import causal_visible_pairs
+
+__all__ = [
+    "MODEL_TYPE",
+    "MODEL_TYPES",
+    "parse_layer_pattern",
+    "normalize_layer_pattern",
+    "check_all_moe_layers",
+    "parse_window_size",
+    "hf_sliding_window",
+    "causal_visible_pairs",
+    "MAKE_VOCAB_SIZE_DIVISIBLE_BY",
+    "vocab_size_with_padding",
+]
+
+# The Primus model_type (one value: the trainer, get_model_provider and the patch condition
+# compare against it; ``muse_spark_text`` is only the HF text_config's model_type, which the
+# checkpoint hook maps to this family).
+MODEL_TYPE = "muse_spark"
+MODEL_TYPES = (MODEL_TYPE,)
+
+# The presets' make_vocab_size_divisible_by (202048 = 64 * 3157), used when the args set none
+# (the converter's own default; Megatron's argument default is 128).
+MAKE_VOCAB_SIZE_DIVISIBLE_BY = 64
+
+
+def vocab_size_with_padding(vocab_size, divisible_by=MAKE_VOCAB_SIZE_DIVISIBLE_BY, tp=1):
+    """The embedding / output-layer rows: ``vocab_size`` rounded up to ``divisible_by``.
+
+    The training ``build_args`` patch and the checkpoint converter both use this, so a
+    converted checkpoint has the training shape. Unlike Megatron's own padding
+    (``divisible_by * TP``), TP is not a factor: the rows depend only on the model config,
+    so one checkpoint loads at every TP. The vocab-parallel layers need the rows to divide
+    by TP; that is checked here (202048 rows divide by every TP that 128 heads / 16 query
+    groups allow) and an error names the fix.
+    """
+    multiple = int(divisible_by)
+    if multiple < 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"make_vocab_size_divisible_by={divisible_by!r} must be >= 1")
+    rows = -(-int(vocab_size) // multiple) * multiple
+    tp = int(tp or 1)
+    if rows % tp:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"padded vocab {rows} (vocab_size {vocab_size} rounded up to make_vocab_size_divisible_by="
+            f"{multiple}) does not divide by tensor_model_parallel_size={tp}: set "
+            f"make_vocab_size_divisible_by to a multiple of {tp}"
+        )
+    return rows
+
+
+# Upper bound on a pattern list (far above any real depth); stops e.g. "[1]*1000000000".
+MAX_PATTERN_LEN = 4096
+# Upper bound on a pattern string (a 4096-entry literal list is ~12k characters).
+MAX_SOURCE_LEN = 4 * MAX_PATTERN_LEN
+_SHOWN_PATTERN_CHARS = 80  # how much of a bad pattern string an error shows
+
+
+def _repeat(lst, n):
+    # n itself is bounded too: an empty list times a huge n would pass the length check
+    if n < 0 or n > MAX_PATTERN_LEN or len(lst) * n > MAX_PATTERN_LEN:
+        raise ValueError(f"layer-pattern repetition {len(lst)}*{n} is outside [0, {MAX_PATTERN_LEN}]")
+    return lst * n
+
+
+def _eval_node(node):
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Expression):
+        return _eval_node(node.body)
+    if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and isinstance(node.value, int) and not isinstance(node.value, bool):
+        return node.value
+    if isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp) and isinstance(node.op, ast.USub):
+        operand = _eval_node(node.operand)
+        if not isinstance(operand, int):
+            raise ValueError("unary minus applies to an int only")
+        return -operand
+    if isinstance(node, (ast.List, ast.Tuple)):
+        out = [_eval_node(e) for e in node.elts]
+        if any(isinstance(v, list) for v in out):
+            raise ValueError("nested lists are not a layer pattern")
+        if len(out) > MAX_PATTERN_LEN:
+            raise ValueError(f"layer pattern longer than {MAX_PATTERN_LEN}")
+        return out
+    if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp) and isinstance(node.op, (ast.Mult, ast.Add)):
+        left, right = _eval_node(node.left), _eval_node(node.right)
+        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add) and isinstance(left, list) and isinstance(right, list):
+            if len(left) + len(right) > MAX_PATTERN_LEN:
+                raise ValueError(f"layer pattern longer than {MAX_PATTERN_LEN}")
+            return left + right
+        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult) and isinstance(left, list) and isinstance(right, int):
+            return _repeat(left, right)
+        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult) and isinstance(left, int) and isinstance(right, list):
+            return _repeat(right, left)
+    raise ValueError(f"unsupported layer-pattern expression: {ast.dump(node)}")
+
+
+def parse_layer_pattern(value):
+    """``value`` as an int, a flat list of ints, or None (strings are parsed safely).
+
+    Raises ValueError for anything else (bools, nested lists, bad syntax, too long).
+    """
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        raise ValueError(f"layer pattern must be an int or a list, got {value!r}")
+    if isinstance(value, int):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        src = value.strip()
+        if len(src) > MAX_SOURCE_LEN:
+            raise ValueError(f"layer-pattern string longer than {MAX_SOURCE_LEN} characters")
+        try:
+            return _eval_node(ast.parse(src, mode="eval"))
+        except SyntaxError as e:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"cannot parse layer pattern {value[:_SHOWN_PATTERN_CHARS]!r}: {e.msg}"
+            ) from None
+        except (MemoryError, RecursionError) as e:  # deeply nested input
+            raise ValueError(f"layer pattern {value[:_SHOWN_PATTERN_CHARS]!r} is nested too deeply") from e
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+        if len(value) > MAX_PATTERN_LEN:
+            raise ValueError(f"layer pattern longer than {MAX_PATTERN_LEN}")
+        out = []
+        for v in value:
+            if isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, int):
+                raise ValueError(f"layer-pattern entries must be ints, got {v!r}")
+            out.append(v)
+        return out
+    raise ValueError(f"layer pattern must be an int, a list or a string, got {type(value).__name__}")
+
+
+def normalize_layer_pattern(value, num_layers, name="layer pattern", warn=None):
+    """Parse ``value``, validate the whole pattern, then cut a list to ``num_layers`` entries.
+
+    An int (every N-th layer) must be in ``[1, num_layers]`` (``num_layers`` unknown: >= 1).
+    A list must be non-empty, every entry (also those past ``num_layers``) must be 0 or 1,
+    and it must have at least ``num_layers`` entries; ``num_layers`` must be a positive int
+    when ``value`` is a list. A cut calls ``warn(message)`` when ``warn`` is given. Every
+    ValueError names ``name``.
+    """
+    source = value
+    try:
+        value = parse_layer_pattern(value)
+    except ValueError as e:
+        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {e}") from None
+    layers_ok = not isinstance(num_layers, bool) and isinstance(num_layers, int) and num_layers >= 1
+    if isinstance(value, int):
+        if value < 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name}: an int means every N-th layer and must be >= 1, got {value}")
+        if layers_ok and value > num_layers:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"{name}: every {value}-th layer is outside num_layers={num_layers} "
+                f"(the int must be in [1, {num_layers}])"
+            )
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        if not value:
+            shown = f" ({source!r} has 0 entries)" if isinstance(source, str) else ""
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} is an empty list{shown}; it needs num_layers={num_layers} entries")
+        if any(v not in (0, 1) for v in value):
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} entries must be 0 or 1, got {sorted(set(value))}")
+        if not layers_ok:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name}: a per-layer list needs num_layers >= 1, got {num_layers!r}")
+        if len(value) < num_layers:
+            raise ValueError(f"{name} has {len(value)} entries, fewer than num_layers={num_layers}")
+        if len(value) > num_layers:
+            if warn is not None:
+                warn(
+                    f"{name}: the pattern has {len(value)} entries; num_layers={num_layers} keeps "
+                    f"the first {num_layers} (a depth-reduced build). Check num_layers if this "
+                    f"is not intended."
+                )
+            value = value[:num_layers]
+    return value
+
+
+def check_all_moe_layers(moe_layer_freq, num_layers):
+    """Muse Spark has a MoE MLP in every layer: ``moe_layer_freq`` must mean "all layers".
+
+    The layer spec builds every layer as MoE (the released model has no dense layer), so
+    any other value would be ignored by the model while FLOPs / memory estimates used it.
+    Accepts None (unset), 1, or a list (or list string) of all ones. Raises ValueError otherwise.
+    """
+    value = normalize_layer_pattern(moe_layer_freq, num_layers, "moe_layer_freq")
+    if value is None or value == 1 or (isinstance(value, list) and all(v == 1 for v in value)):
+        return
+    raise ValueError(
+        f"Muse Spark builds a MoE MLP in every layer: moe_layer_freq must be 1 "
+        f"(or all ones), got {moe_layer_freq!r}"
+    )
+
+
+_WINDOW_RE = re.compile(
+    r"\s*(?:\(\s*({p})\s*\)|\[\s*({p})\s*\]|({p}))\s*".format(p=r"[-+]?\d+\s*,\s*[-+]?\d+")
+)
+
+
+def parse_window_size(value):
+    """``window_size`` as a causal pair ``(left, 0)`` of ints, or None.
+
+    Accepts None, a 2-element list / tuple of ints, or a string of exactly one pair:
+    ``"(2048, 0)"``, ``"[2048,0]"`` or ``"2048,0"`` (yaml / CLI). Checked: ``left`` is
+    -1 (no limit) or >= 0, and ``right`` is 0 (Muse Spark attention is causal). Anything
+    else (nesting, unbalanced brackets, empty or extra items, floats, bools) raises a
+    ValueError that names ``window_size``. The config and the FLOPs patch both use it.
+    """
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(value, str):
+        m = _WINDOW_RE.fullmatch(value)
+        if not m:
+            raise ValueError(f"window_size must be one pair '(left, right)' of ints, got {value!r}")
+        parts = [int(p) for p in next(g for g in m.groups() if g).split(",")]
+    elif (
+        isinstance(value, (list, tuple))
+        and len(value) == 2
+        and all(isinstance(p, int) and not isinstance(p, bool) for p in value)
+    ):
+        parts = list(value)
+    else:
+        raise ValueError(f"window_size must be a pair (left, right) of ints, got {value!r}")
+    left, right = parts
+    if left < -1:
+        raise ValueError(f"window_size[0] must be -1 (no limit) or >= 0, got {left}")
+    if right != 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"Muse Spark attention is causal: window_size[1] must be 0, got {right}")
+    return left, right
+
+
+def hf_sliding_window(value):
+    """HF ``sliding_window`` (keys incl. the query) from a ``window_size`` in the presets'
+    HF convention: the parsed ``left``, or None for no window (None / ``left == -1``).
+    ``left == 0`` raises (an HF window counts the query, so it is >= 1)."""
+    ws = parse_window_size(value)
+    if ws is None or ws[0] == -1:
+        return None
+    if ws[0] < 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"window_size[0] is an HF sliding_window and must be >= 1 (or -1), got {ws[0]}")
+    return ws[0]
